title: Kinch, the knife-blade
html_source:
Mulligan’s nickname for Dedalus is “Kinch.” Kinch is a form of Kinchin, which means child.

This meaning is significant in the context of this chapter and its predecessor book Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man. Stephen did his best to free himself from his roots and his parents and emigrated to Paris, but due to the death of his mother he returned and therefore is confronted with his dependence on his parents (and his roots).

“Knife-blade” lends some aggression to the name Kinch. It is not unlikely that Mulligan alludes to the fact that Stephen tries to behave as independently from his parents as possible, thereby hurting them (cf. the passage where Mulligan says that Stephen refused to pray at his mother’s deathbed).
